function: Blind receive beamforming against interference: a linear beamforming layer is optimized to maximize a pre-trained CNN classifier's confidence in the signal of interest (p. 1, 4).
system: Receive ULA, N=4 elements at half-wavelength spacing in simulation (915 MHz); ORBIT testbed ULA with N=4 at 5.4 GHz; narrowband; no RIS (p. 3, 6, 11-12).
method: Supervised pre-trained 1D CNN binary classifier (frozen) with trainable linear beamforming layer optimized by SGD with momentum per snapshot; transfer learning, temperature-scaling calibration (p. 4-6).
data_channel: Training: synthetic single-antenna noisy 16-QAM IQ, 2x10^6 samples augmented to 10^5 waveforms; testing: simulated ULA data with calibration errors and ORBIT over-the-air captures (p. 6-7, 11-12).
test_conditions: Classifier trained on single-antenna 16-QAM at 915 MHz; tested on simulated arrays (samples, SNR, N=2-10) and over-the-air at 5.4 GHz without retraining (p. 6-12).
baselines: Non-learned: optimal, LSE, LS-CMA, P-SCORE, JADE, cFastICA, SOBI beamformers. Learned: none; earlier ML beamformers [23]-[25] not compared (p. 2, 8).
metrics: Median array SINR (ASINR) versus samples, SNR, antennas; convergence rate; runtime; bit error ratio in over-the-air test (p. 7-12).
complexity: Classifier parameters cut from 11936kappa+1034 to 1184kappa+249, operations from about 1984kappa*L to 832kappa*L; measured CPU runtimes in ms per method (p. 6, 9-10).
openness: none: only a plan to release code and datasets upon publication, no link (p. 3).
q1_support: p. 11: "we validate the performance from Section IV-D by processing over-the-air signals collected using the ORBIT testbed [29] without retraining the classifiers used by the CBTL beamformer". Measured data used for testing; pre-training is synthetic (p. 6); see notes.
q2_support: p. 12: "without retraining them for the larger clock offsets at 5.4 GHz, multipath propagation, or hardware imperfections"; training band: p. 6: "The carrier frequency was fc = 915 MHz"
q3_support: p. 8: "The BSS-based beamformers included implementations of JADE [42], cFastICA [43], and SOBI [44] with their default parameters"; p. 2: "the existing techniques for blind beamforming require training data from (or generated by a model of) an antenna array". Missing: any earlier learned beamformer as baseline.
q4_support: p. 6: "the number of parameters from 11936κ + 1034 to 1184κ + 249"; p. 9: "while measuring the runtimes of the uninformed beamformers as N and L were varied" (Table III, p. 10).
q5_support: p. 3: "We plan to release our code and datasets to the public upon publication of this paper". Missing: any link or DOI; the ORBIT captures are the authors' own (p. 11) and the classifier is trained on synthetic data (p. 6).
notes: Borderline points for the reviewer. (1) Eligibility: the learned element is a pre-trained CNN classifier used as the objective of a per-snapshot iterative weight optimization (p. 4); kept as included because the classifier's learned features define the beamformer, the function is receive beamforming with a 4-element array (area 3, main metric ASINR, p. 7), and the paper has no jamming or classification-only task. (2) q1 is 1 only through the ORBIT over-the-air captures used to test the beamformer (p. 11-12); the classifier is pre-trained on synthetic data and the main simulations use a custom array model, so a reviewer who requires training on measured data should set q1 to 0. (3) q3 is 0: JADE, cFastICA and SOBI are classical ICA or second-order blind source separation algorithms, although the paper calls blind source separation an unsupervised learning approach (p. 1); no neural or trained beamformer is compared. (4) q5 is 0: the release is only planned (p. 3); the measured-data clause of q5 was not applied because the captures are unreleased own data and the classifier is not trained on them.
